newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower, shrugs off Inco strike.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower, shrugs off Inco strike.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker amid little news, moderate volume and a further technical correction, as the strike at Canada's Inco failed to boost prices, dealers said.

Trading was light and there is some disappointment that stocks on LME rose slightly, but it was too early to say if this was because of a summer seasonal slowdown approaching, Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said.
"If the Inco strike continues for any period of time, it may lend support to the market," Raptopoulos said.
July COMEX copper settled down 1.45 cents at 115.65 cents a lb, traded 116.40 to 114.90 cents. Spot June went out 1.50 cents lower at 115.60 cents.

Inco's Sudbury complex, where workers have been on strike since Tuesday, produces about 90,000 tonnes of copper a year, helping to supply the North East and Midwest U.S. markets which remain fairly tight with strong premiums.
The average premium in the U.S. Mint tender for copper Tuesday was 3.25 cents per pound.
Striking unions at Inco said Wednesday the dispute affecting Sudbury copper and nickel operations, may last several months.
Inco said Tuesday the strike will not affect deliveries to customers for at least one to two months.
LME stocks rose 50 tonnes Wednesday to 132,550 tonnes, while the London exchange's cash to three months backwardation ended at $55/$60, recovering from a low of $48/$53 early in COMEX's session.
